problem.title: Your tools show what already happened. None of them says what to do tomorrow.
problem.body: You have analytics, ads, a CRM and ChatGPT. They all do tasks. None of them answers the Monday question: what do we do now, and how will we know it worked?
symptoms: Marketing runs on impulse: ads one week, a post the next
You copy what worked at another company and hope it fits yours
More time spent fiddling with tools than selling
At the end of the month, nobody can say what brought the customers in
problem.stakes: Companies rarely stop growing for lack of tools. They stop because nobody tested the right thing — or wrote down what it taught them.

what.title: It decides what to do. Your tools keep doing the doing.
what.lead: Growing is not a task list. It is a cycle: decide, test, measure, learn, decide again. AUREA keeps everything it knows about your business, picks the next test, writes the plan, then reads the result so the next choice is better.

pillars.title: It remembers your business
pillars.body: Your product, your customers, your market and everything you have already tried live in one place.
pillars.result: You never explain your company again from scratch.

pillars.title: Every idea becomes a test with a target
pillars.body: Each suggestion arrives complete: what to do, where, for how long, and which number has to move.
pillars.result: You always know what you are testing and when you can call it a win.

pillars.title: A miss becomes knowledge too
pillars.body: Win or lose, the result is recorded and goes into the next decision.
pillars.result: From the tenth test on, the suggestions are tailored to your company.

loop.title: Seven steps. And it never stops.
loop.lead: Set it up once and you have a process instead of a task list. Every lap around the cycle makes the next decision better.

items.title: Goal
items.body: You say what you want: more customers, more revenue, a lower cost per sale. In plain words.

items.title: Research
items.body: AUREA studies your market, your competitors and your audience — and shows where each finding came from.

items.title: Plan
items.body: It comes back with two or three possible routes, with pros, cons and how much work each one is. You choose.

items.title: Test
items.body: The chosen route becomes a ready-made test: what to do, where, for how long, and which number has to move.

items.title: Do it
items.body: Your team (or your tools) puts it into practice. The start and end dates are recorded on the test, along with the number to watch.

items.title: Measure
items.body: At the end, the number is compared with the target you agreed on at the start. No dressing it up.

items.title: Learn
items.body: The result is saved. The next cycle starts knowing what worked and what did not.

items.title: The analyst

contrast.body: A chat AI answers the question you remembered to ask. A metrics dashboard shows what already happened. AUREA holds your goal, picks the next test, and settles the account at the end: it worked, or it did not.

contrast.stackNote: AUREA replaces none of them. It tells you what each one should be doing this week.

faq.title: What everyone asks before creating an account.

items.q: Is this different from just using ChatGPT?
items.a: It is. ChatGPT answers what you ask and forgets your business the moment you close the tab. AUREA keeps what it knows about your business, picks the next test on its own, writes the plan with a number to watch, records the result and uses it in the next decision. One writes text. The other runs the process.

items.q: Do I need to know marketing to use it?
items.a: No. You speak in business terms: I want more customers, I want to spend less per sale. AUREA turns that into research, a plan and a test, and explains every difficult word inside the product itself.

items.q: Does AUREA do things in my name?
items.a: No. It suggests and you approve. Nothing is published, sent or spent outside AUREA without you clicking. Every suggestion can be edited before it becomes a test.

AUREA is in early access, so there is no customer average to show yet — and we are not going to invent one. What the first session gives you is concrete: research on your market with sources, two or three possible routes, one test with a target and a deadline, and an honest record of the result when it comes in.

items.q: Does it work with the tools I already use?
items.a: Yes. Your analytics, your CRM and your ad platforms stay where they are, and you are the one acting in them — AUREA decides what to do with them. Automatic connections are on the roadmap, not ready yet, and nothing breaks if you switch tools.

items.q: What does it cost, and what is a credit?
items.a: Starting is free: 50 credits, one company, no card. A credit is one AI task — a market research run costs 5, a set of routes 3, a test 2. Plans start at R$ 297 a month, with credits that renew every month.

items.q: What if there is little public information about my market?
items.a: AUREA shows what it found with the source and tells you what it could not find. You see the gap instead of a confident-sounding guess, and you can fill it with what you already know about your industry.
Yes. What you write stays in your account, stored encrypted, and is never used to train anyone else’s AI.

trust.title: Built by a founder who got tired of guessing.
trust.body: I used to jump between analytics, ChatGPT, spreadsheets and advice from the internet to decide what to do each week — and I could never tell whether any of it had worked. AUREA is the system I wanted: it decides, tests, measures and remembers. Growing should be a process you can trust, not a bet you keep repeating.

railHelp.STRATEGY: How you intend to reach the goal — the growth mechanism and the channels.
railHelp.EXPERIMENT: A bounded, measurable test of one belief, with a metric, a target and success criteria. Completing it is not the same as it working.
railHelp.OUTCOME: What actually happened: the measured value of the experiment's metric.
railHelp.LEARNING: What the outcome means, stated so it can improve the next decision. You validate it before AUREA relies on it.

autoPlan.help: AUREA designs the test for each hypothesis: name, metric, channel, audience and success criteria. The number you start from, the target and the dates are yours — a made-up baseline would later be read as a real measurement.
autoPlan.short: Not enough credits for the whole batch.
autoPlan.partial: {{count}} hypothesis was left out. Try again to cover what is missing.
autoPlan.partial_other: {{count}} hypotheses were left out. Try again to cover what is missing.
autoPlan.createFailed: The test was designed, but it could not be created.

experiments.title: Tests
experiments.help: A deliberate attempt to move one metric, with a hypothesis behind it and a success criterion decided before it starts. That is what separates an experiment from activity.
experiments.subtitle: Every test checks one hypothesis against one number.
experiments.emptyHint: An experiment always tests a hypothesis, so start from a strategy: open one, add the hypothesis you want to test, then design the experiment for it.
experiments.actionFailed: Could not apply that change. Try again in a moment.
experiments.metricHelp: The one number this experiment is trying to move. Picked before it starts, so the result cannot be re-argued afterwards.
experiments.baselineHelp: Where the metric stood before the experiment. Without it a target is just a number — there is nothing to compare against.
experiments.targetHelp: The value that would make this experiment worth having run.
experiments.successHelp: What counts as a win, written down before the result is known. This is what stops a disappointing outcome from being reinterpreted as a good one.
experiments.newSubtitle: One hypothesis, one metric, and what would count as success — decided now, not after the result.
experiments.needHypothesis: There is no hypothesis worth testing yet. An experiment always tests a hypothesis, so write the hypothesis first: open a strategy and add it there.
experiments.hypothesisSelect: Choose the hypothesis this experiment tests
experiments.name: Name
experiments.namePh: Plain-text first touch to ops leads
experiments.successPh: At least 8 calls booked in 3 weeks
experiments.createFailed: Could not create the experiment. Try again in a moment.

cancel.title: Cancel this experiment?
cancel.body: A cancelled experiment cannot be reopened or restarted, and it will produce no outcome to learn from. This action cannot be undone.

outcomes.title: Measured outcomes
outcomes.help: A number that was actually measured after the experiment ran, with the day it was observed and where it came from. Without those two, a number cannot be trusted months later.
outcomes.observedAtHelp: The day the number was true, not the day it was typed in. Leave it blank for today. A date in the future is refused: an observation that has not happened yet is not an observation.
outcomes.cost: {{credits}} credit for AUREA to read the result
outcomes.cost_other: {{credits}} credits for AUREA to read the result
outcomes.short: Not enough credits for the reading. You can still record the number — the reading can wait.
outcomes.recordedWithoutInterpretation: Number recorded. The reading did not run: {{reason}}
outcomes.recordFailed: Could not record that measurement. Try again in a moment.

next.measure: This experiment is finished. Record what it measured — until there is a number, it produced nothing to learn from.
next.learn: There is a measurement. Write down what it taught you: that is what makes the next experiment better than this one.

learnings.title: What we learned
learnings.help: What the measurement taught you, written as a claim someone could disagree with. A candidate is not knowledge: it becomes knowledge only when a human validates it.
learnings.titlePh: Ops leads reply, but only to plain text
learnings.statementPh: Plain-text first touches booked 9 calls; the templated ones booked none.
learnings.proposeFailed: Could not save that learning. Try again in a moment.
learnings.actionFailed: Could not apply that change. Try again in a moment.

reject.title: Reject this learning?
reject.body: A rejected learning cannot be proposed again, and AUREA will not reason from it. This action cannot be undone.

archive.title: Archive this learning?
archive.body: An archived learning cannot be reopened. Archive it once it no longer describes the business. This action cannot be undone.

binding.title: Where this number comes from
binding.help: Which metric of your data source answers for this experiment's metric. Your metric name is your own words; this is the name the source understands. Without a binding, you keep typing the number in by hand — nothing breaks.
binding.metricHelp: The technical name the source uses, like `conversions` or `activeUsers`. It has to be one the property actually has.
binding.filterHelp: Optional. Narrows the metric to part of what it counts — for example the field `eventName` with the value `sign_up`, so only sign-ups are counted.
binding.aiNothingFits: AUREA found no metric in this property that answers for this experiment. Nothing was filled in.
binding.bothFilterFields: Fill both filter fields, or neither.
binding.notConnected: No data source is connected yet.

measurement.title: What the source measured
measurement.help: Where this number came from: which property, which query, which period. AUREA reads it; you confirm it. A number nobody agreed with is not a result.
measurement.zero: The source answered zero for this period. That is a measurement, not a failure — but it is also what broken tracking looks like, so check the period before confirming.
measurement.orManual: Or type a different number below.
measurement.noBinding: This experiment does not say where its number comes from yet, so there is nothing to read.
measurement.noSource: No data source is connected, so there is nothing to read.
measurement.noPeriod: This experiment has no start and end dates, and without a period there is nothing to measure.
measurement.notReady: AUREA reads the number once the experiment is over.

interpret.title: What the result means
interpret.helpText: AUREA reads your recorded outcomes back against the baseline and the target, suggests what might explain them, and drafts a learning. It never decides whether the experiment succeeded — that judgement stays yours.
interpret.failed: AUREA could not read this result. Try again.
interpret.notReady: Complete the experiment and record an outcome first.
interpret.accepted: Saved. Validate it when you are confident.

hypotheses.help: A belief stated so it can be wrong: what you think will happen, to whom, and why. An experiment is how you find out.
hypotheses.title: Hypotheses — what we will test
hypotheses.empty: No hypotheses yet. Write down what you believe will work and why — that is what an experiment tests.
hypotheses.statementHelp: Phrased so it could turn out false: who, what changes, and in which direction. "Ops leads reply more to a plain-text first touch" can be wrong; "improve outreach" cannot.
hypotheses.statementPh: Ops leads reply more to a plain-text first touch
hypotheses.confidenceHelp: How sure you are before testing. Low confidence is not a reason to skip it — a cheap test of a doubtful belief is often the most informative one.
hypotheses.createFailed: Could not add the hypothesis. Try again in a moment.
hypotheses.actionFailed: Could not apply that change. Try again in a moment.

reject.title: Reject this hypothesis?
reject.body: A rejected hypothesis cannot be reopened, and any experiment still testing it loses its purpose. This action cannot be undone.

billing.title: Billing & credits
billing.subtitle: Your plan, your credits, and where they went.
billing.help: Your organization subscribes; every workspace in it gets the plan's monthly credits. Buying a pack adds credits that never expire.

plans.title: Plans
plans.help: The plan sets how many credits each workspace gets per month and how many workspaces you can create.
plans.changed: Plan changed. The new allowance is already available.
plans.ownerOnly: Only the organization owner can subscribe or change the plan. Ask them to do it.

packs.title: Credit packs
packs.help: Credits you buy once. They do not expire, do not renew, and stay spendable even if the subscription is canceled.
packs.adminOnly: Only an owner or admin can buy credit packs. Ask one of them to do it.

allowance.title: Monthly allowance
allowance.help: Credits included in your plan for this workspace. They reset every month and do not roll over.
allowance.exhausted: Allowance used up for this period.

credits.title: Credits
credits.help: Every AI run costs credits. The allowance comes with your plan and resets monthly; purchased credits never expire.
credits.workspaceScope: These credits belong to the workspace you are in, not to the whole organization.

billing.trialNotice: You are on trial: the plan allowance is zero until you subscribe. Your welcome credits still work.
billing.pastDueNotice: A payment failed. Your allowance stays for now while the card is retried — update it to avoid losing it.
billing.canceledNotice: The subscription is canceled, so the monthly allowance is zero. Credits you purchased are still spendable.
billing.portalHelp: Opens Stripe, where you can change the card, see invoices, or cancel.
billing.notConfigured: Billing is not available in this environment.
billing.actionFailed: Could not start that action. Try again in a moment.

ledger.title: Statement
ledger.help: Every credit that came in or went out, newest first: AI runs that spent credits, refunds, purchases and grants.
ledger.empty: Nothing here yet. Every agent run will show up in this statement.

return.confirmed: Payment confirmed. Your plan and credits are up to date.
return.pending: Payment received. The confirmation can take a moment.

learnings.title: Learnings
learnings.subtitle: Everything your tests have taught you, in one place you can read back.
learnings.help: A conclusion drawn from a test that already ran. Confirmed learnings feed AUREA’s next suggestions — that is how it gets sharper each time around.
learnings.empty: Nothing learned yet. Run a test, record the result, and the learning shows up here.

company.intro: Tell AUREA who you are — start with the basics, then enrich with your brand identity.

help.businessEssentials: Basic information that identifies your company in AUREA. Name is required.
help.companyName: Your legal or trading name as customers know it.
help.industry: The sector or vertical your company operates in.
help.valueProposition: The core promise your company delivers to customers.
help.positioning: How you want your company to be perceived in the market relative to competitors.
help.foundedYear: The year your company was founded.
help.headquarters: City and country where your company is based.
help.fundingStage: Current funding status of your company.
help.mission: Your company's mission statement — why you exist.
help.vision: Your aspirational long-term vision for the company.
help.brandVoice: Describe how your brand communicates — tone, style, personality.
help.values: Core values that guide your company culture and decisions.

company.websiteError: Must start with https:// or http://

placeholder.valueProposition: e.g., Cut support costs in half without hurting customer satisfaction
placeholder.positioning: e.g., The specialized growth automation tool for B2B SaaS
placeholder.mission: e.g., Empower every SaaS business to achieve sustainable growth through AI...
placeholder.vision: e.g., Become the global standard for AI-powered growth operations...
placeholder.brandVoice: e.g., Professional but approachable, data-driven, optimistic...

help.logo: Upload your company logo (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or SVG). This helps AUREA personalize the experience.

help.documents: Upload PDFs, Word docs, or plain text files that describe your company, products, or market (e.g., pitch deck, business plan, whitepapers). AUREA uses these to understand your context.

products.intro: What products or services does your business offer? This helps AUREA understand what you are selling and to whom.
products.empty: No products added yet. Add your first product to get started.
products.tip: 💡 Tip: The more specific you are about what makes your product different, the better AUREA can recommend strategies that leverage that uniqueness.

help.productName: The name of your product or service as customers know it.
help.description: A clear, concise description of what this product does. Focus on the outcome it delivers.
help.targetAudience: Who is this product specifically for?
help.differentiator: What makes this product unique compared to alternatives?
help.pricingModel: How do you charge for this product?
help.pricePoint: Typical price or price range (e.g., "9/mo" or "Starting at 00")
help.status: Whether this product is live, in beta, planned, or discontinued.

placeholder.description: e.g., AI-powered growth operating system that turns goals into strategies and experiments
placeholder.differentiator: e.g., Only tool that combines context + strategy + execution + learning in one loop

competitive.intro: Understanding your competitive landscape helps AUREA identify opportunities where competitors are weak.
competitive.name: Name
competitive.tip: 💡 Tip: AUREA will use competitor weaknesses to identify opportunities where you can win.

help.differentiator: In one sentence, what makes you different from all competitors? This is your core positioning.
help.marketPosition: Where do you sit in your market relative to competitors?
help.competitors: List 2-5 main competitors. Focus on direct competitors, not the entire market.
help.advantages: What do you do better than competitors? Be specific (e.g., "2x faster onboarding" vs just "easy to use").
help.positioning: How this competitor positions itself in the market.
help.threatsFromCompetitors: Specific risks competitors pose to your business (e.g., "Aggressive pricing", "Faster feature releases").

placeholder.differentiator: e.g., Only growth tool that combines AI strategy + execution + learning in one loop
placeholder.name: Competitor name

market.intro: Market context helps AUREA understand the size of the opportunity and where the market is heading.
market.tip: 💡 Tip: Market trends and opportunities help AUREA recommend timely strategies that ride market momentum.

help.tam: The total market demand for your product/service. All potential customers globally.
help.sam: The segment of TAM you can reach with your current product and channels.
help.som: The portion of SAM you can realistically capture in the near term (1-3 years).
help.growthRate: How fast is your market growing annually? E.g., 15 = 15% per year.
help.maturity: What stage is your market in?
help.trends: What macro trends are shaping your market? (e.g., "Remote work", "AI adoption")
help.opportunities: External factors creating opportunities for growth (e.g., "New regulation requiring our solution")
help.threats: External risks or challenges in your market (e.g., "Economic downturn", "New competitor funding")

constraints.intro: Knowing your constraints helps AUREA recommend realistic strategies that fit your resources and timeline.
constraints.tip: 💡 Tip: Honest constraints help AUREA avoid recommending strategies you cannot execute. A founder-only team needs different tactics than a 20-person team.

help.budget: How much can you spend per month on growth activities (ads, tools, content, etc.)?
help.teamSize: How many people work at your company?
help.growthTeam: How many people work on growth full-time? (0 if just founder)
help.urgency: How urgent is growth right now? This affects strategy recommendations (quick wins vs. long-term).
help.capabilities: What can your team do in-house? (e.g., "Build landing pages", "Write code", "Design graphics")
help.limitations: What cannot you do yet? (e.g., "Cannot ship to EU", "No phone support", "No mobile app")

performance.intro: Current performance gives AUREA baseline metrics to measure improvement against.
performance.tip: 💡 Tip: These baseline metrics help AUREA calculate ROI and recommend strategies that improve your unit economics.

help.mrr: Your predictable monthly revenue from subscriptions.
help.arr: MRR × 12, or total annual recurring revenue.
help.activeCustomers: Customers who used your product recently (e.g., last 30 days).
help.churn: Percentage of customers who cancel each month. E.g., 5 = 5%.
help.signups: Average number of new signups per month.
help.cac: Average cost to acquire one paying customer.
help.ltv: Average revenue you make from a customer over their lifetime.
help.ltvCac: LTV divided by CAC. Healthy SaaS is typically 3:1 or higher.
help.conversion: Percentage of signups that become paying customers. E.g., 2.5 = 2.5%.
help.timeToConvert: Average days from signup to becoming a paying customer.
help.baselineDate: The date these metrics were measured as of. Lets AUREA compare future progress against this exact snapshot.
help.channels: Where your customers come from today.

activities.intro: Understanding what you are doing now helps AUREA avoid duplicate recommendations and build on existing momentum.
activities.tip: 💡 Tip: AUREA will build on what is working and suggest how to scale or optimize existing channels before recommending entirely new ones.
activities.doneTitle: You are done with the context wizard!
activities.doneMessage: Click "Save & Finish" below. AUREA now has rich context to reason about your growth. The more complete this is, the better its recommendations will be.

help.channels: What channels are you actively using today? (e.g., "SEO", "LinkedIn organic", "Google Ads", "Email")
help.content: How much content are you producing regularly?
help.paid: Are you running paid ads? If so, where and how much?
help.partnerships: Strategic partnerships for growth (e.g., "Integration with Salesforce", "Co-marketing with CompanyX")
help.other: Anything else you are doing for growth that does not fit above (e.g., "Community building", "Webinars", "Events")

projects.intro: Growth projects with clear objectives. Each project can have multiple measurable goals.
projects.empty: No projects yet. Add your first growth project.

help.objectives: Define 1-3 measurable objectives for this project. Each objective should have a clear metric and target.
help.metric: What you are measuring for this objective (e.g., "trial-to-paid conversion", "monthly signups").
help.baseline: Where this metric stands today, before the project starts.
help.target: Where you want this metric to be by the deadline.

placeholder.description: Brief description of the project scope and goals

campaigns.intro: Marketing and outreach campaigns linked to projects, with measurable KPIs.
campaigns.empty: No campaigns yet. Add your first campaign.

help.linkedProject: Optionally link this campaign to a specific project for traceability.
help.targetAudience: Who is this campaign targeting? Describe the persona or segment.
help.kpis: Define measurable KPIs for this campaign (e.g., impressions, clicks, conversions, sign-ups).
help.kpiTarget: The number this KPI needs to reach for the campaign to be considered a success.
help.kpiCurrent: The KPI's latest known value — update it as the campaign runs.

placeholder.description: Brief description of the campaign strategy and target
placeholder.targetAudience: e.g., B2B SaaS founders in Latin America
